reasons: Section 2.2 is a sole-source exclusivity that restricts which hosted analytics services Customer may buy (and arguably build), with no product-level scope, no cap and no carve-outs — squarely a field-of-use restriction on our side, correctly flagged as a deviation from the preferred position and consistent with the 'high' severity.

The redline deletes the entire one-sentence clause, which is the playbook's preferred remedy and the minimal edit available for a standalone exclusivity sentence; no residual restriction on Customer remains and both deterministic checks pass.

The comment is accurate, uses the required prefix and first-person-plural tone, states what changed and why, and offers the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) without lecturing.

Minor: the comment's cross-references to Sections 2.1 and 12.3 are not verifiable from the supplied paragraphs, but they are consistent with the rationale and do not affect the validity or direction of the edit.
